title: Physical Security Specialist (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811), DC I&L
raw_text:
5.     MOS 5814, Physical Security Specialist (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811), DC I&L

    a. Summary. A Physical Security Specialist is a Military Policeman
additionally trained to provide commanders the ability to conduct risk/
vulnerability assessments, analyze crime, and recommend appropriate courses
of action to eliminate conditions conducive to terrorism, espionage,
sabotage, wrongful destruction, malicious damage, theft, and pilferage.
Asset protection and loss prevention can be accomplished through all these,
but not limited to a physical security program, electronic security system
program, and a loss prevention program.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have obtained the grade of corporal or higher.

            (2) Must currently hold and maintain all prerequisites of PMOS 5811.

    c. Requirements.    Complete the Conventional Physical Security Course
(A1681P3), U.S. Army Military Police School.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and
Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Police and Sheriff's Patrol Office 33-3051.

       f.   Related Military Skill.    None.

CORRECTIONS 1. Introduction. The Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections OccFld provides the installation commander continuous support by enforcing the law, preventing and suppressing crime, assessing command physical security posture, preserving military control, quelling disturbances, investigating offenses, apprehending offenders, protecting property and personnel, investigating traffic accidents, controlling traffic, providing first response to active shooters incidents and special response to a barricaded subject, guarding military prisoners and supervising brig operations and correctional custody units. Provide the MARFORRES Commander support to security and mobility operations, battlefield circulation and traffic control, rear area security operations to include limited offensive and defensive combat operations, detention operations to include handling and safeguarding prisoners of war, refugees, or evacuees, guarding military prisoners, and returning absentees/deserters to military control.

5. MOS 5814, Physical Security Specialist (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811), DC I&L a. Summary. A Physical Security Specialist is a Military Policeman additionally trained to provide commanders the ability to conduct risk/ vulnerability assessments, analyze crime, and recommend appropriate courses of action to eliminate conditions conducive to terrorism, espionage, sabotage, wrongful destruction, malicious damage, theft, and pilferage. Asset protection and loss prevention can be accomplished through all these, but not limited to a physical security program, electronic security system program, and a loss prevention program. b. Prerequisites (1) Must have obtained the grade of corporal or higher. (2) Must currently hold and maintain all prerequisites of PMOS 5811. c. Requirements. Complete the Conventional Physical Security Course (A1681P3), U.S. Army Military Police School. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
